Professionals guide

Professional indemnity insurance: who needs it?

Chestnut Insurance Agency editorial team · Published 21 November 2026

Anyone whose clients rely on their advice, design or services should consider professional indemnity (PI) insurance. It does not stop a client complaining, but it helps pay for the defence and, where covered, the compensation.

Who should consider PI

Some regulators, professional bodies or clients require PI. Even where it is not required, a single claim can be larger than a small practice can absorb.

  • Doctors, dentists and clinic owners
  • Engineers, architects and surveyors
  • Accountants, auditors and tax advisers
  • Advocates and law firms
  • Consultants, IT firms and other advisers

How a claim might arise

A miscalculation in a structural design. A missed filing deadline. Advice that a client says caused a financial loss. In each case, the client alleges that the professional fell below the expected standard. The allegation alone costs time and legal fees.

Understand claims-made cover

Many PI policies respond to claims first made during the policy period, and may only cover work done after a retroactive date. If you change insurers or stop practising, ask how earlier work will remain covered. Gaps here can leave you exposed.

What to check before buying

  • The services described in the policy match what you actually do
  • The limit of indemnity is suitable for your largest client or contract
  • The excess is affordable
  • Whether defence costs sit inside or outside the limit
  • Retroactive date and notification of circumstances conditions
  • Exclusions that matter to your profession

What PI does not do

It does not cover injury or property damage claims, which belong under public liability, and it does not cover dishonest acts or fines and penalties. It also depends on accurate disclosure.

This guide is general education about insurance in Kenya. It is not legal or financial advice and does not describe any specific policy. Policy wording, exclusions and the law that applies at the time govern. Speak to an advisor about your situation.
